text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- The Swiss government details its plans to turn state-run Swiss Federal Railways into a joint-stock company in early 1998.
- A new law requires police personnel in Basel, Switzerland's second bigest city, to wear name tags when in uniform.
- Swiss beers lost market shares to imported beers for the fifth year in a row in the 1995/96 brewing year that ended on September 30.
- The number of company bankruptcies in Switzerland rose by 9.1 percent to 3,468 in the first 10 months of the year, compared to the same period in 1995.

- Some 150 employees of Neuenburger Insurance, a subsidiary of Winterthur Insurance in French-speaking western Switzerland, will lose their jobs when Winterthur takes over all of Neuenburger's business and phases out the unit next year.

- French magazine "Le Nouvel Observateur" reports that 337 tonnes of Nazi gold confiscated by Allied forces after World War Two have been quietly divided up and turned over to nine European countries.
- Electronics group LEM posted a 5.5 percent drop in profit to 0.6 million Swiss francs for the first nine months of the year. JOURNAL DE GENEVE
- Following the Zurich Insurance group, Winterthur Insurance announced it will restructure its Swiss operations.
